name: Rice Cakes
description: Historical recipe from Miss Leslie's Complete Cookery (1851). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: and a half of flour
ingredients.originalText: a pint and a half of flour

ingredients.name: quarter of a pound of butter
ingredients.originalText: a quarter of a pound of butter

instructions.text: Pick and wash half a pint of rice, and boil it very soft
Drain it, and let it get cold
Sift a pint and a half of flour over the pan of rice, and mix in a quarter of a pound of butter that has been warmed by the fire, and a salt-spoonful of salt
Beat five eggs very light, and stir them gradually into a quart of milk
Beat the whole very hard, and bake it in muffin rings, or in waffle-irons
Send them to table hot, and eat them with butter, honey, or molasses

source.author: Eliza Leslie
source.originalInstructions:
1. Pick and wash half a pint of rice, and boil it very soft
2. Drain it, and let it get cold
3. Sift a pint and a half of flour over the pan of rice, and mix in a quarter of a pound of butter that has been warmed by the fire, and a salt-spoonful of salt
4. Beat five eggs very light, and stir them gradually into a quart of milk
5. Beat the whole very hard, and bake it in muffin rings, or in waffle-irons
6. Send them to table hot, and eat them with butter, honey, or molasses
